prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Practice Companion Controls", "Try basic desktop pet shortcuts while your companion prepares in the background.", "Select Command to Test"]
1: ["Your pet graphics are compiling in the background. It is safe to keep working on your desktop."]
2: ["Desktop Pet Ready to Launch", "Review your companion shortcuts below to start interacting on your screen.", "Alt+P to Show/Hide | Right-Click for Settings | Drag to Move"]
3: ["Customize Desktop Controls", "Select your preferred shortcut to invoke and hide your desktop pet.", "Preferred Shortcut Key"]
4: ["Sign In to Restore Existing Pets", "Logging into your account automatically retrieves your saved companions, items, and settings."]
5: []
6: ["Ensure your photo is well-lit and front-facing for optimal desktop rendering.", "Upload & Create Companion"]
7: ["Find Your Companion Match", "Answer two quick questions to discover your ideal desktop pet archetype.", "Desktop Style Quiz"]
8: ["Finalizing companion certificate details. Your selections are safely saved."]
9: ["Welcome to Your Desktop Companion", "Follow 4 simple steps to adopt, customize, and place your pet on your desktop."]

verdicts.problem: Asks for personal information by requesting a user photo.
